subject: Adding a smoother affects model prediction study

messages.author: f3d71ca39a57d9c3
messages.subject: Adding a smoother affects model prediction study
parts:
Hi folks,

I hope you're all keeping well.

I'm running a model of skate presence (very zero-inflated, across the NE Atlantic shelf, this has become the story of my life at this point).

To validate the model I'm running a simulation study (according to Zuur et al., 2017) to simulate 1000 response datasets from model betas, and then compare the number of zeros in the simulated datasets with that of the observed data.

For the initial model formulation (f1), the observed zeros are right in the middle of the histogram of simulated zero counts (no problems there)

U <- 1 # priors for the temporal component, start with 1 and see how it looks. It worked ok this time
hyper.prec.year = list(theta = list(
  prior = "pc.prec",
  param = c(U, 0.01)))

f1 <- y ~ -1 + Intercept + dcoast.std + btemp.std + bath.std + current.std + xkm.std + ykm.std + haul_dur.std +
  f(quarter, model = "rw2") + f(survey, model = "iid") +
  f(year, model = "rw1", scale.model = TRUE, hyper = hyper.prec.year)

B1 <- inla(f1,
           family = "binomial",
           data = inla.stack.data(est),
           control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, cpo= TRUE, config= TRUE),
           control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(est)))

However when i include an additional smoother for a variable (f2), the proportion of zeros in the simulated data far exceeds that of the observed. 

f2 <- y ~ -1 + Intercept + dcoast.std + f(inla.group(btemp.std), model="rw2") + bath.std + current.std + xkm.std + ykm.std + haul_dur.std +
  +   f(quarter, model = "rw2") + f(survey, model = "iid") +
  +   f(year, model = "rw1", scale.model = TRUE, hyper = hyper.prec.year)

B2 <- inla(f2,
           family = "binomial",
           data = inla.stack.data(est),
           control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE, config = TRUE),
           control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(est))) 

I've been playing around with INLA for a few years now, and any time I've come up against the issue I'm left scratching my head (sometimes its due to the spatial effect and priors etc, but this time I've left out the spde completely). Does anyone have an explanation for what this output means? Is it related to the variation within the model itself? Is it a sign of overfitting somehow?

Thanks in advance for any advice you guys have :)
Sophie
